text:
Nila: Noticed a customer report: embeddings p95 jumps when small (64/128) and large (1024/1536) dims are batched together. Probable cause: runtime kernel switch.
Jon: Do we have a quick repro or example payload?
Nila: Yes, attached in the ticket. Ingress packer favors fill-bytes which mixes dims to maximize GPU utilization.
Sam: That explains it. Splitter isn't invoked unless clients call /split or preflight signals. Our packer doesn't consider dim-uniformity.
Priya: Two prongs: add a routing hint header so clients can request dim-homogeneous routing; or tweak packer to prefer homogeneous batches above X bytes.
Jon: Header idea: `x-rd-embed-route: homogeneous` (optional). Ingress router honors if tenant flag enabled.
Sam: Need telemetry: `embed.batch_dim_variance` tag and `route_hint` dimension. Helps correlate to p95.
Priya: Billing edge: homogeneous pools may change unit efficiency. Expose `unit_factor` in preflight so console quota chart matches expectation.
Nila: Console owners: show toggle with estimated multiplier and short explanation. Also surface canary status.
deploy-bot: feature-flag `routing.dim_hints` created in staging.
Jon: Proposed rollout: 1) header + metrics (this week), 2) preflight unit_factor API (next week), 3) console toggle + canary (week after).
Sam: Canary: 5% sample, monitor p95 and cost delta. Alert if p95 doesn't improve >3%.
Priya: SDKs should ignore unknown headers. I'll own runtime heuristic; Jon owns telemetry + canary; Nila owns console copy/docs.
Nila: I'll open the tracking ticket and link the customer trace.
Jon: I'll draft a short RFC and add the initial dashboard mock for the heatmap.
Priya: Great, thanks.
Nila: Thanks team, follow-ups in the ticket. :thumbsup:
